answers.answer: An Exile who takes the Oathkeeper title during Act cannot win as Usurper at the next Wake: at the start of that Wake, the Exile victory check occurs while they are still Oathkeeper, and only afterward do they flip to Usurper. They may first win at the following Wake, provided they still hold the title, or at the end of round 8 if that arrives first while they remain Usurper. Losing the title prevents the win; if they later retake it, the title resets to Oathkeeper and the sequence starts again.
answers.evidence: Scoring / Victory Conditions, ‘Usurper victory has two timing windows’: ‘next Wake check (not yet Usurper), then flip to Usurper, then win at the following Wake’ and ‘Losing title prevents this win; retaking resets it to Oathkeeper.’

answers.answer: Supremacy matches Conquest; People matches Rebellion; Protection matches Sanctuary; Devotion matches Faith. For a Visionary win, an Exile must have the true Vision revealed, complete its goal at Wake, and the global Visions Drawn count must be at least 3. For Conquest and Sanctuary, ‘most’ means strictly more than every other player, so a tie does not count. The summary does not separately state a tie rule for Rebellion or Faith Vision goals.
answers.evidence: ‘Oathkeeper title and four Oaths’ table lists all four matches. ‘Visionary victory’ says the Exile needs the revealed true Vision, goal completed at Wake, and at least 3 global draws; it defines Conquest/Sanctuary most as strictly more than every other player.

answers.answer: At the ends of rounds 5, 6, and 7, roll only if the Chancellor or a Citizen is Oathkeeper. The game ends on 6 in round 5, 5–6 in round 6, or 3–6 in round 7. An Exile holding the Oathkeeper title prevents the roll. Round 8 ends automatically. An Exile Oathkeeper cannot permit a round 5–7 roll.
answers.evidence: ‘Stable regime’: ‘at ends of rounds 5, 6 and 7, roll end die only if Chancellor or Citizen is Oathkeeper’; thresholds 6 / 5–6 / 3–6; ‘An Exile Oathkeeper/Usurper prevents the roll.’

answers.answer: At the end of round 8: (1) if Chancellor or Citizen is Oathkeeper, Empire wins, with a qualifying Citizen Successor winning alone instead of the Chancellor; (2) otherwise an Exile Usurper wins; (3) otherwise a qualifying revealed Exile Vision wins, with simultaneous qualifying Visions prioritized Conquest, then Rebellion, then Sanctuary, then Faith; (4) otherwise Empire wins, with a qualifying Successor replacing the Chancellor. A Citizen does not win by Vision or Usurper status.
answers.evidence: ‘War exhaustion’ gives the four-step round-8 priority and Vision order; ‘Citizens/Chancellor cannot win by true Visions or Usurper.’

answers.answer: Citizen Successor goals: under Supremacy, hold more relics plus banners than the Chancellor and every other Citizen; under People, hold Darkest Secret; under Protection, hold People's Favor; under Devotion, hold Grand Scepter. A Citizen cannot win by a revealed Vision or by becoming Usurper.
answers.evidence: ‘Oathkeeper title and four Oaths’ table lists each Citizen Successor goal. ‘Visionary victory’ states Citizens/Chancellor cannot win by true Visions or Usurper.

answers.answer: At Wake, if you hold People's Favor, choose to put 1 favor from your board onto it or return 1 favor from it to the least-full suit bank, choosing among tied least-full banks. Never remove its last favor: if it has 1, add one if able; if you have no favor, do nothing. On the Mob side, repeat that choice once. After the choice or choices, check whether it has at least 6 favor and flip it to Mob if so. If it becomes Mob at this final check, that Wake does not retroactively get another payment.
answers.evidence: Wake step 1 specifies the two choices, last-favor rule, repeating once when Mob, and the 6+ threshold checked afterward; it says a banner becoming Mob at that step does not retroactively repeat payment.

answers.answer: Rest order: (1) return favor on denizens/edifices to matching suit banks; (2) return secrets on denizens/edifices/relics to your board and flip your facedown board secrets faceup; (3) refresh Supply—Exiles and Chancellor by their remaining personal-bank warband count, while a Citizen copies the Chancellor marker's exact space, including the leftmost; (4) save each unspent Supply by moving the marker one extra space left per unspent Supply, capped at the leftmost space; (5) optional Rest powers, each once in an order you choose.
answers.evidence: ‘Rest: mandatory order’ enumerates these five steps and says Citizen refreshes to the exact Chancellor marker space; saved Supply moves left per unspent Supply, capped at leftmost.

answers.answer: Search either the world deck or the discard pile for the pawn's region, never both. A discard-pile Search costs 2 Supply. World-deck Search costs 2 when zero Visions have been drawn, 3 at 1–2, and 4 at 3–5; Darkest Secret replaces that world-deck cost with 2, with other modifiers still applying. Draw up to 3, one at a time from the world deck; a world-deck Vision must be announced, immediately stops the draw, and advances Visions Drawn by 1. A Vision drawn from a discard pile neither stops drawing nor advances the track.
answers.evidence: ‘Search — 2–4 Supply’ specifies sources and costs, one-at-a-time world draws, and the different effects for a world-deck Vision versus a discard-pile Vision.

answers.answer: A discarded card goes facedown atop the next region's pile in the cycle Cradle → Provinces → Hinterland → Cradle, never its own region pile. For a hand/adviser card, use the pile based on your pawn's region; for a card discarded from a site in another region, use the cycle based on that card's region. Favor on a discarded card immediately returns to its matching suit bank; secrets go to the acting player's board facedown.
answers.evidence: ‘Discard destinations’ gives the region cycle and specifically says a card at a site in another region uses that card's region; it states where favor and secrets go.

answers.answer: Advisers are limited to 3 total, counting both faceup and facedown; before playing over the limit, discard an adviser subject to locks, and check a limit-changing incoming card against the new limit. Facedown advisers have no suit, restriction banner, or power; any card can be held facedown. Later, a facedown adviser can be played faceup to a legal destination or discarded as a minor action. A faceup adviser cannot be discarded at will and may be discarded only when a rule permits or requires it, respecting locks. An Exile may play a true Vision faceup into the separate Revealed Vision slot, replacing and discarding the previous revealed Vision; it is not an adviser. Chancellor/Citizens may hold true Visions facedown but cannot reveal them.
answers.evidence: Search options and Adviser retention table specify limit/state and later options; True Vision option specifies Exile-only reveal in separate slot replacing old Vision.

answers.answer: Muster costs 1 Supply. At your pawn's site, choose an empty denizen or intact edifice (no favor or secrets already), place 1 favor on it, and take 2 warbands from your personal bank onto your board; a Citizen takes purple warbands. You need not rule the site. Relics and ruins are ineligible, and a remote site cannot be used. Trade also costs 1 Supply and uses an empty denizen/intact edifice at your pawn's site. For 1 secret placed on the card, gain 1 favor plus 1 for each matching faceup adviser from that card's suit bank. Or place 2 favor on the card to gain 1 secret per matching faceup adviser from the shared bank. Facedown advisers do not match; with no matching advisers, the second option yields zero secrets, though its 2-favor cost remains payable. Finite favor/warband supplies limit gains to what is available; secrets are unlimited.
answers.evidence: ‘Muster — 1 Supply’ and ‘Trade — 1 Supply’ specify eligible cards, costs, gains and destinations, including no-match and limited-supply cases.

answers.answer: Recover costs 1 Supply plus the target cost. A relic must be facedown at your site; pay its printed site cost (3 favor to the indicated bank, burn 2 favor, burn 1 secret, or burn 2 secrets), then hold it faceup in your personal bank. You cannot Recover a player-held relic or one in the Reliquary. Either banner can be Recovered from anywhere, including yourself or the shared bank, by paying an amount strictly greater than the banner's current resources. For People's Favor, put the paid favor on it, distribute its old favor one at a time among suit banks beginning at a bank of your choice and proceeding in bank order away from the world deck, wrapping as needed; flip it to normal side if Mob, with no seizure penalty. For Darkest Secret, put the paid secrets on it; the new holder takes 1 old secret and the previous holder gets the rest. If recovering it from yourself, all old secrets return to you; if from the shared bank, the remainder stays there.
answers.evidence: ‘Recover — 1 Supply plus target cost’ gives relic eligibility and costs, then the People's Favor and Darkest Secret bullets specify strict outbids and old-resource destinations.

answers.answer: To Recover another player's Darkest Secret, their pawn's site must contain at least one suited card whose suit matches none of that player's faceup advisers. If they have no faceup advisers, any suited site card meets that condition, so the Secret is recoverable. An empty site or a ruin-only site has no suited card and protects the Secret. Recovering your own Secret or one in the shared bank ignores this protection.
answers.evidence: ‘Darkest Secret protection, corrected by official errata’ states the at-least-one unmatched suited-card condition, and explicitly covers no faceup advisers, empty sites, ruins and self/shared-bank recovery.

answers.answer: For a Campaign, choose another player who rules your site or whose pawn is there as defender; if no player rules your site, you may choose bandits. At least one target must be at your pawn's site, and if the defender rules that site, you must target it. You may add any of the defender's sites anywhere on the map, one defense die per site. If the defender's pawn is at your site, you may also target any of their relics there (printed defense dice), banners there (dice equal to resources on the banner), or their pawn and favor together (2 dice). A co-located relic target itself satisfies the local-target requirement.
answers.evidence: Campaign steps 1–2 state defender selection, mandatory local target, remote sites, and co-located relic/banner/pawn-and-favor targets and dice.

answers.answer: The attacker selects up to as many attack dice as warbands in the attacking force, after relevant modifiers. Defense is shields rolled, doubled for each double-symbol (multipliers stack), plus all defending warbands at targeted sites and the defender's board force if their pawn is at the attacker's site or a targeted site; doubles multiply shields only. Bandits add 1 per targeted bandit site. Each attack skull immediately kills one warband from the attacker's force. Count full swords, plus one for each pair of hollow swords; an odd leftover hollow sword adds zero. The attacker may sacrifice surviving force warbands for +1 attack each, but if sacrificing must sacrifice exactly enough to win, never extra. Attack must strictly exceed defense; a tie or lower is a defender win.
answers.evidence: Campaign steps 2, 4 and 5 detail attack dice, defense formula, skulls, hollow swords, sacrifices and strict win threshold.

answers.answer: On an attacker victory, first the defender kills half of the warbands in its defending force, rounded down, and returns the rest to board; resolve defeated battle-plan effects. The attacker may then place any number, including zero, of surviving force warbands on any targeted sites. Zero leaves a site to bandits unless another power applies. The attacker takes all targeted relics and banners; for a banner seized by a method other than Recover, burn 2 banner resources down to a minimum of 1, and People's Favor flips to Mob. If pawn-and-favor was targeted, the attacker may force the defender to travel to a legal chosen site without Supply and may independently burn half the defender's board favor, rounded down. Shrouded Wood can override the attacker's destination choice if its enemy ruler chooses the forced destination. The summary does not provide a separate procedure named banishment; it only describes this forced travel as a target resolution.
answers.evidence: Campaign steps 6–8 specify casualties, target resolution, zero garrisons, banner seizure and forced travel. They do not describe a distinct banishment procedure.

answers.answer: When an Imperial player defends, the Chancellor automatically joins as Ally. Other non-attacking Citizens may join if permitted by the defender and their pawn is at the attacker's site or a targeted site. Apply modifiers ruled by defender/Allies; treat powers' ‘you,’ ‘your enemy,’ and ‘defender’ as the whole defending side, while ‘your site/board’ still refer to each user's own. Allied board warbands add defense only when the Ally's pawn is at the attacker site or a targeted site. Defenders/Allies may use plans at Imperial sites and their own advisers, not other players' advisers. A shared plan can be used once total, by one user who pays; the declared defender resolves disagreements over order, timing, priority, and user. Chancellor chooses which Imperial defenders' warbands die; surviving site warbands go to Chancellor's board and surviving Citizen board warbands stay on those boards. An intra-Empire Campaign does not make every Citizen non-Imperial. A Citizen attacking Chancellor or another Citizen is non-Imperial for that Campaign; when Chancellor attacks a Citizen, that Citizen is non-Imperial for it.
answers.evidence: Campaign ‘Imperial defense’ bullets state Ally participation, shared powers, plan access/one-use, decision authority, casualty destinations and status; Campaign step 1 gives the non-Imperial exceptions.

answers.answer: Base Travel Supply costs by origin and destination region: from Cradle, Cradle 1, Provinces 2, Hinterland 4; from Provinces, any region costs 2; from Hinterland, Cradle 4, Provinces 2, Hinterland 3. Travel is to any different site, not just an adjacent one. If the destination is facedown, reveal it, place its printed favor/secrets from the shared bank, and place its printed relics facedown beside it from the relic deck. Apply the fixed-number cost first, then other increases/decreases. A Free Travel power that says to spend no Supply is the final override, even over an increase. Entry restrictions still apply unless ignored by a power.
answers.evidence: Travel table lists base regional costs; paragraph below says reveal/stock destination and fixes cost order, final free override, and entry restrictions.

answers.answer: The Grand Scepter holder cannot offer Citizenship on the turn they took the Scepter. On a later turn, its holder may offer it to any Exile, including themself, and must promise exactly one Reliquary relic; they may also negotiate a binding exchange of favor, secrets, banners, and non-Reliquary relics, and may allow the recipient to peek at Reliquary relics. On acceptance, the recipient flips to Citizen, replaces all their own board/map warbands with purple (choosing which to remove/replace if purple is insufficient), discards their revealed Vision, flips Usurper to Oathkeeper, ends their Act if it is their turn, and refreshes to full leftmost Supply. They exchange the promised pieces, and the Chancellor gains the newly uncovered mandatory Reliquary modifier. The summary also says an offer cannot be made the turn its current Scepter holder took it.
answers.evidence: ‘Citizenship and exile during play’ describes Scepter timing, offer gift and optional binding exchanges, then acceptance effects and mandatory modifier.

answers.answer: For the next Oath, a winner whose victory came by Vision alone must use the Oath matching that Vision. A winner by another method or multiple methods chooses any Oath except the current one. For Chronicle Citizenship, if the winner is an Exile, first flip every Citizen board, including boxed boards, to Exile; then the winner may offer Citizenship to other Exiles except those just flipped. No Reliquary gift, resource payment, or Scepter permission is needed for these Chronicle offers. Each accepting Exile flips their board to Citizen and replaces every garrison at every site they rule with exactly one warband of the winner's color. Rebuild the world deck with 10 denizens plus 2 random Visions in the top stack (12 cards), 15 denizens plus the remaining 3 Visions in the next stack (18 cards), then remaining denizens below. The aid's ‘12 denizens + 2’ is an acknowledged misprint; the summary specifies 10 denizens + 2 Visions, so the top stack is not 14 cards.
answers.evidence: Chronicle steps 1–2 specify Oath selection and Citizen-to-Exile turnover/Chronicle offer procedure; step 9 specifies 10+2 and 15+3 stacks and identifies the aid's 12+2 as incorrect.
